citations.quote: my flatmate has been ill a lot lately, coughing and tired, but honestly we don't know if that's the flat or just her job at the daycare
we have condensation running down the walls and mould on all the window frames.
the underfloor heating there hasn't come on at all since spring, the thermostat just blinks
the guy from the tenants' association said with a dispute like that you need an expert to check where the damp comes from
I'm not going to stop paying rent or put it in a deposit thing, I don't want trouble.
I am writing to you as the tenant of the above flat to ask you to arrange an inspection of my flat as soon as possible.
We acknowledge that there is a problem in your flat and apologise for the delay.
Our caretaker will visit to assess the problem. We propose 15 September 2026 at 4 p.m. for access to the flat.

plan.because: Needed to establish the parties, property and tenancy terms.
The May letter requests an inspection but does not identify the reported defects.
The August reply acknowledges a May report, but does not establish the date it was received.
Needed to document the visible defects, locations and dates.
The reply records a proposed visit but not the subsequent response, proposed work and access history.
Mould is reported; dated moisture and temperature observations are relevant.
The underfloor heating fault is reported; inspection findings are needed.
Symptoms are reported; any connection to the flat remains uncertain.
An expert inspection is reported as needed to investigate the disputed damp cause.
The customer says she does not intend to deposit rent.
This document is optional under the process.

questions: Are the symptoms or cold creating an immediate health or safety concern requiring urgent assistance?
When did the landlord receive the defect report, and is there another report describing the mould and heating fault?
What happened during and after the caretaker's visit, and has any repair or further access been arranged?
